FAKE CREDIT APPLICATIONS

By: Nicky Troll | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Crooks make off with millions of Rands worth of products using legitimate companies details to get credit – leaving a trail of deception and suppliers out of pocket.

Unique Selling Point:
- CAUTIONARY TALE
- EXPOSING THE LEVEL OF DECEPTION CREATED BY FRAUDSTERS
- NEW CRIME TREND PERFECTLY EXECUTED

Summary:
Criminal Syndicates are going all out to get their hands on products – duping suppliers into giving them credit using legitimate companies details.

Suppliers dot all the I’s and cross all the t’s in an attempt to vet these applications – but what do you do when the credit bureaus you employed to check the dodgy company gave the green light to do business with them.


Further information:
OUR CASE STUDY
THE VICTIM: MICAN INDUSTRIAL SUPPLIES, a medium sized business
THE CON: Supplied PPE goods valued at R585 955.83 to fraudsters in December 2020 on credit.
THE ROGUES: Fraudsters posing as ONE WORLD SHINING, a legitimate company with a good credit rating.

WHAT HAPPENED:
MICAN were contacted by One World Shining (OWS) to supply them with PPE goods. OWS wanted to apply for a credit account and completed a MICAN application form.

MICAN in turn sent the credit application details to Accountability – a 3rd party credit check service – who make use of TransUnion Reports and supply clients with a report on an Accountability Document.

THE OUTCOME OF THE CREDIT CHECK:
OWS passed as a bank code C, For R1.5 million. Rating: Good account, Low Risk. Trade references, were all Excellent! Spending between R350 000 up to R12 million. No judgments or defaults on any trade reference.

So MICAN went ahead with order. The goods were delivered and they waited for payments. But almost 6 weeks later they started to get suspicous and uncovered they had been scammed.

TRAIL OF DECEIT
Not just MICAN. There are at least 3 other comapines that have been scammed. And a further 3 that flagged the applications and did not go through with the purchase order.

In the space of a few weeks the FAKE One World Shining applied for credit at the following companies that we know of:
• WELDING EQUIPMENT to the value of R400 000
• ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT to the value of R500 000
• SUGAR
• OFFICE SUPPLIES
• And then MICAN’s PPE worth 600 000

DISCREPANCIES
The fraudulent OWS’ company address: 82 Pretoria Road, Sandton.
The real OWS company address: 52 Planet Avenue, Unit 21 Chestnut Warehouse, Crown Mines

MICAN were told to send the PPE goods to a warehouse and not the Sandton address. The address for the warehouse is; Unit 1, East Borough Business Park, 15 Olympia Street, Eastgate, Sandton.

When MICAN went to the warehouse address, they were met by a gentleman by the name of Khaya Radebe, cell phone 067 090 0549, Mr Radebe informed them that he simply works there and has no idea as to who is operating from there, he however signed all 3 of MICAN’s invoices? The property is owned by Tuluze Consulting.

CAN THE REAL MR YOUSAF PLEASE STAND UP
The details for One World Shining Pty Ltd were hacked(stolen) from a Mr Abdul Qadir Yousaf ID. #: 7611106173187. A certified copy of an ID book is sent to suppliers with the credit applications – the picture in the ID is fake.

Mr Yousaf had laid a case at the SAPS in October of 2020 because his details were being used fraudulently. Case #: CAS155:11/2020 at the Langlaagte police station. The fraudsters used a fake ID with the picture of another man in it to get passed the credit checks.

The real Mr. Yousaf has agreed to an interview – he says there have been a number of companies contacting him about this con.

SKIRTING ACCOUNTABILITY
On the company website Accountability describes itself as a web-based service that was created “with the aim of “protecting” businesses by reducing the risk caused by outstanding payments”.

Our Value Proposition
“By becoming a valued Member of Accountability, you will have access to a variety of services whereby you can accurately determine potential clients’ creditworthiness before extending them the required trade credit.”

Mission Statement: Accountability is the dominant web-based service team aiming to protect SME’s and Corporates by providing them with tools to reduce credit risk and report Consumer and Commercial credit behaviour to registered Credit Bureaus.

When I spoke to them – they say they merely provide clients with the informationon TransUnion Reports and they are not responsible for that. It seems the fraudsters have managed to get past TransUnion and CIPC and no one is taking responsibility.

In Accountability’s T&Cs it states that the subscriber takes all liability. I contacted attorney Reggie Tshabalala who believes it’s not simple when Accountability was providing an expert service. I have sent him the contract and report and will hopefully find out more soonest.


COMPANY ID THEFT RIFE
Christo Snyman, VP of the International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators (IAFCI) in South Africa, has noted a spike in this type of crime trend. “From our conversations with suppliers, we have discovered that the number of credit applications being made using false or stolen information, has become a massive problem.”

Being a victim of identity fraud, which can have a massive negative impact on a company if the situation is not immediately reported and handled correctly.

Snyman said that there is a very real need for businesses to become more aware of the prevalence of fraud, and to act when they become aware of fraudulent activity.
“Firstly, if you conduct business on credit, never assume the accuracy of a client’s information – always check the validity of the information that they provide. Check that names and contact details are correct, and double check banking details by calling the applicant or customer. In the case of long-standing customers, be especially wary of changes in contact or banking details.”

In addition, Snyman said that all businesses must have a policy of reporting any fraudulent activity. “It is very unfortunate that so many companies still choose to let cases of attempted fraud go unreported. Even if it might seem unlikely that the fraudsters will be caught, it is still important to notify police. At the same time, businesses should let other companies in their network know if they become aware of a new scam, or if their identity had been stolen.”

- THE REAL MR YOUSAF

- TRACKING AND TRACING ELEMENT

FINAL SCRIPT: FAKE CREDIT APPS

VO: Criminals have taken smoke and mirrors to the next level - with an onslaught of fake credit applications targeting businesses in an already strained economic climate.

LINK: Fraudsters hijack legitimate companies’ details, apply for credit and make off with hundreds of thousands of Rands worth of stock – leaving only a trail of deception and suppliers out of pocket.

VO: These syndicates target suppliers of commodities that are quick to move on the black market.

In November last year, Michelle Linaker’s Industrial Supply company had a credit application from a new client for Personal Protective Equipment.

MICHELLE: We were approached by the company, One World Shining, they // followed the procedure, we gave them the credit application.

VO: After the applicant submitted all the required documents, Linaker did a Commercial Search on the company registration number via a web-based service - Accountability.

MICHELLE: The deciding factor was that the report was fantastic, // They say to us that the account was good for us to give them credit, up to two million. And there was no default. There was no judgment. That was perfect.

VO: The report also included sections on business identification, company registration details, a bank code summary and trade references amonst others.

MASA: In your mind, had you done due diligence?
MICHELLE: Absolutely, I mean, we are paying for a service and we are trusting our business in the hands of Accountability to ensure that what they are doing is correct and // we rely on those reports in order to guide us on whether or not we'll open an account for a customer

VO: The order was delivered in three batches to a warehouse in Eastgate, Johannesburg.

With no payments, Linaker realized that they’ve been scammed - but it was too late, the stock was gone.

MICHELLE: It's devastating. Six hundred thousand rand is a lot of money and our business is compromised, integrity's compromised. all cell phone numbers that we had for contact with people were disconnected.

VO: Christo Snyman is from the International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators. He has noted a spike in this evolving crime trend.

CHRISTO: It's a full time job. That's what they do every day. And, you know, if you get used to the fact that you can make money, easy as they have been doing and a lot of times not not getting arrested or prosecuted, you know, why would you go and and do something else?

LINK: These syndicates will go to great lengths to appear authentic – even forking out cash for office space in plush suburbs. The FAKE One World Shining went as far as setting up offices in Sandton, paying R76 000 for two month’s rent and deposits.

VO: This particular syndicate, posing as the REAL One World Shining, had done credit applications for around R80 million targeting electronics companies, asphalt suppliers, welding equipment suppliers, sugar distributors and stationary companies to name a few .

These fraudsters were so brazen they even met with sales reps tasked with vetting the company before granting credit.

Kobus Coertze works for a local sugar supplier and distributor – he met with them in Sandton.

KOBUS: I thought it for legitimate business. I was met by a receptionist, very professional, contacted the person to tell them I'm here for the appointment with people sitting at desks working like a normal business.

VO: Even though credit was approved, Coertze’s company decided to put the brakes on when the first order for R900 000 came through.

KOBUS: The owners looked at the financials….. realised something might be wrong.

VO: They informed the fraudsters they would only grant credit after three months of cash orders.

KOBUS: //they ask me to reconsider and we were firm with our decision to say not at all cash. And after that, I never heard from them again.

CHRISTO: That these criminals do not have a fixed addresses, they constantly change cell phone numbers and they use fraudulent email domains// they know that the time in doing their fraudulent scam is shortlived so they need to do it quickly and they need to very organized

VO: The offices in Sandton had been vacated and the fraudsters had disappeared.

LINK: This is the warehousing facility where suppliers were told to deliver goods – it’s in an industrial area, surrounded by other warehouses – looks legit – let’s go see if there’s anyone around…

VO: We met the owner Yusuf Jamal and the accounts manager, Khaya Radebe at Tuluze Consulting.

KHAYA: We also tried to find these guys
MASA: Why tyring to find
KHAYA: because they also have an account, an outstanding balance with us as well // we never received a cent.

VO: The goods from 4 different companies valued at over 1 million rand were received and distributed from this address. Both Jamal and Radebe claim they were just the unwitting middle men and are owed R70 000 for warehousing services provided to the FAKE One World Shining.

MASA: You guys have any idea where these goods went,
KHAYA: with the emails they communicated, they would say these goods are going to Zimbabwe, they're going to visit us
MASA: but never an actual physical address,
KHAYA: No.

VO: Tuluze Consulting say they too were duped by the paper work the fraudsters supplied for the credit application – it looked real – from the CIPC documents to the SARS Clearance Certificate, the financials and even a certified copy of the director’s ID.

But just because it’s certified, doesn’t mean it’s real.

While the ID number is correct – this is not Abdul Qadir Yousaf – this is. He is not from India, but from Pakistan.

This is not the One World Shining letterhead, this is.

This is also not the One World Shining website, this one is .

The actual business address is in Crown Mines , not in Sandton.

We met the real Abdul Yousaf at his actual warehouse, where he’s been operational for 5 years.

MR YOUSAF: I do an import and export. I never, ever take any credit from in South Africa, any store.// But this guy is a fraud guy. I don't know who's that one, but my company is good company

VO: Yousaf first became aware of the fraud in late October when he was contacted by a so-called unpaid supplier. He immediately opened a case with the police.

MR Yusuf: // Because now I'm too angry // Because I never do any fraud // in my company
MASA: But it seems like it was you.
MR Yusuf: Yeah, people think it's because it's my company, // we are sitting here. [We never do any fraud.] If we were doing fraud so we can’t sit here. You understand? We just ran away from you.

MASA: Who do you blame for this loss?
MICHELLE: I blame accountability // we relied on them. We paid them for a service and we relied on what they gave us. And I blame them completely.

VO: Accountability, members are promised “access to a variety of services whereby you can accurately determine potential clients’ creditworthiness before extending them the required trade credit.”

The incorrect Sandton address along with the incorrect contact details used by the FAKE One World Shining were included in the Accountability Commercial Search Report pulled by Mican in November 2020.

Accountability Group director, Devon Kemp spoke to us from Cape Town.

DEVON: The nature of our business is purely risk mitigation. We are the dominant web service. aiming to protect SMEs & corporate by providing them with tools to reduce the credit risk.
MASA: Would you say that this is an expert service that you provide?
DEVON: I would say, yes,

VO: But the details in the report don’t check out.

LINK: we’ve checked the TRADE REFERENCES in the credit reports – and we either can’t find those companies – and the ones we did track down say they’ve never done business with one world shining

VO: Interestingly a trade reference from a Yusuf at a company listed as Tulze that cannot be traced but is similar to the warehousing company - TULUZE, was included in the report.

YUSUF: I don't know anything about it. I haven't spoken to nobody from any credit reference or anything.

VO: It seems Accountability has some explaining to do.

MASA: I just would like to understand how is this section compiled trade on file?
DEVON: that is subject to investigation Cant DISCLOSE that right now, it’s subject to investigation.// that you have to ask TransUnion directly.
MASA: Are you saying those names come from TransUnion?
DEVON: Well, the data in its entirety that is compiled in this report comes from TransUnion.

 
VO: According to Kemp, Accountability directly sources data from a number of credit bureaus and white labels the information - he claims ,the information is simply rebranded in an Accountability document and insists the clients should verify the information supplied in the reports.

Attorney Reginald Tshabalala, explains it’s not so easy to shift liability when offering a so-called expert service.

REGGIE: whether the source of information is TransUnion or not, first of all, accountability, the contracting party to me. So whether accountability gets its information from third party, it doesn't really matter//. At the end of the day, the document is theirs and their own. They must own it. M7

VO: TransUnion responded in writing. They did not specifically answer the questions we posed. But stated the following:

“We are confident that we followed all applicable procedures in our data collection...”

ANd specifically about the MICAN //ONE WORLD SHINING CASE:
“Our review of this matter shows that Accountability may have omitted from their report or presented differently certain information provided by TransUnion that could have offered additional context to the credit decision.”

MICHELLE: Accountability's blaming TransUnion, TransUnion is blaming accountability, accountability's blaming us as the customer, and nobody to date has even apologized that this has happened to us or taken responsibility, that the trade references that they gave and the report that they gave to us was an excellent account. But in actual fact, it wasn't. C2M24 10.30

MASA: you've provided this document to your clients. Then you find out that this information is incorrect. Should that not surprise you?.
DEVON: That is for the bureau to rectify, it's not for me to justify//. The main thing that I need to get through is that it is powered by the bureau which we state at the bottom.

VO: Kemp is adamant that they are covered by their terms and conditions.

MASA: Are you passing the buck onto TransUnion because you want to take any responsibility or accountability?
DEVON: I cannot take responsibility for information that I did not source
MASA: you provided it to your clients as accurate information and you took their money. // We've established now that it's not accurate.
DEVON: So that's actually quite want a very stern statement,
MASA: FACTUAL a statement, because here is an accountability document that is full of inaccuracies in black and white.
DEVON: OK

 
VO: Accountability and TransUnion claim there were discrepancies between the report and the credit application completed by the FAKE company.

Tshabalala’s advice is that businesses should scrutinize every detail of every transaction.

REGGIE: you are the one who is going to part with goods that you're going to give one credit, it is your responsibility. Don't rely on verification agencies simply because they've got terms and conditions that generally absolve them, // Because if you're going to rely on one verification agency to give you 100 percent information//, you will most likely be disappointed. M14

VO: Christo Snyman is from the International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators. He has noted a spike in this evolving crime trend. CHRISTO: It's a full time job. That's what they do every day. And, you know, if you get used to the fact that you can make money, easy as they have been doing and a lot of times not not getting arrested or prosecuted, you know, why would you go and and do something else? LINK: These syndicates will go to great lengths to appear authentic – even forking out cash for office space in plush suburbs. The FAKE One World Shining went as far as setting up offices in Sandton, paying R76 000 for two month’s rent and deposits. VO: This particular syndicate, posing as the REAL One World Shining, had done credit applications for around R80 million targeting electronics companies, asphalt suppliers, welding equipment suppliers, sugar distributors and stationary companies to name a few . These fraudsters were so brazen they even met with sales reps tasked with vetting the company before granting credit. Kobus Coertze works for a local sugar supplier and distributor – he met with them in Sandton. KOBUS: I thought it for legitimate business. I was met by a receptionist, very professional, contacted the person to tell them I'm here for the appointment with people sitting at desks working like a normal business. VO: Even though credit was approved, Coertze’s company decided to put the brakes on when the first order for R900 000 came through. KOBUS: The owners looked at the financials….. realised something might be wrong. VO: They informed the fraudsters they would only grant credit after three months of cash orders. KOBUS: //they ask me to reconsider and we were firm with our decision to say not at all cash. And after that, I never heard from them again. CHRISTO: That these criminals do not have a fixed addresses, they constantly change cell phone numbers and they use fraudulent email domains// they know that the time in doing their fraudulent scam is shortlived so they need to do it quickly and they need to very organized VO: The offices in Sandton had been vacated and the fraudsters had disappeared. LINK: This is the warehousing facility where suppliers were told to deliver goods – it’s in an industrial area, surrounded by other warehouses – looks legit – let’s go see if there’s anyone around… VO: We met the owner Yusuf Jamal and the accounts manager, Khaya Radebe at Tuluze Consulting. KHAYA: We also tried to find these guys MASA: Why tyring to find KHAYA: because they also have an account, an outstanding balance with us as well // we never received a cent. VO: The goods from 4 different companies valued at over 1 million rand were received and distributed from this address. Both Jamal and Radebe claim they were just the unwitting middle men and are owed R70 000 for warehousing services provided to the FAKE One World Shining. MASA: You guys have any idea where these goods went, KHAYA: with the emails they communicated, they would say these goods are going to Zimbabwe, they're going to visit us MASA: but never an actual physical address, KHAYA: No. VO: Tuluze Consulting say they too were duped by the paper work the fraudsters supplied for the credit application – it looked real – from the CIPC documents to the SARS Clearance Certificate, the financials and even a certified copy of the director’s ID. But just because it’s certified, doesn’t mean it’s real. While the ID number is correct – this is not Abdul Qadir Yousaf – this is. He is not from India, but from Pakistan. This is not the One World Shining letterhead, this is. This is also not the One World Shining website, this one is . The actual business address is in Crown Mines , not in Sandton. We met the real Abdul Yousaf at his actual warehouse, where he’s been operational for 5 years. MR YOUSAF: I do an import and export. I never, ever take any credit from in South Africa, any store.// But this guy is a fraud guy. I don't know who's that one, but my company is good company VO: Yousaf first became aware of the fraud in late October when he was contacted by a so-called unpaid supplier. He immediately opened a case with the police. MR Yusuf: // Because now I'm too angry // Because I never do any fraud // in my company MASA: But it seems like it was you. MR Yusuf: Yeah, people think it's because it's my company, // we are sitting here. [We never do any fraud.] If we were doing fraud so we can’t sit here. You understand? We just ran away from you. MASA: Who do you blame for this loss? MICHELLE: I blame accountability // we relied on them. We paid them for a service and we relied on what they gave us. And I blame them completely. VO: Accountability, members are promised “access to a variety of services whereby you can accurately determine potential clients’ creditworthiness before extending them the required trade credit.” The incorrect Sandton address along with the incorrect contact details used by the FAKE One World Shining were included in the Accountability Commercial Search Report pulled by Mican in November 2020. Accountability Group director, Devon Kemp spoke to us from Cape Town. DEVON: The nature of our business is purely risk mitigation. We are the dominant web service. aiming to protect SMEs & corporate by providing them with tools to reduce the credit risk. MASA: Would you say that this is an expert service that you provide? DEVON: I would say, yes, VO: But the details in the report don’t check out. LINK: we’ve checked the TRADE REFERENCES in the credit reports – and we either can’t find those companies – and the ones we did track down say they’ve never done business with one world shining VO: Interestingly a trade reference from a Yusuf at a company listed as Tulze that cannot be traced but is similar to the warehousing company - TULUZE, was included in the report. YUSUF: I don't know anything about it. I haven't spoken to nobody from any credit reference or anything. VO: It seems Accountability has some explaining to do. MASA: I just would like to understand how is this section compiled trade on file? DEVON: that is subject to investigation Cant DISCLOSE that right now, it’s subject to investigation.// that you have to ask TransUnion directly. MASA: Are you saying those names come from TransUnion? DEVON: Well, the data in its entirety that is compiled in this report comes from TransUnion. VO: According to Kemp, Accountability directly sources data from a number of credit bureaus and white labels the information - he claims ,the information is simply rebranded in an Accountability document and insists the clients should verify the information supplied in the reports. Attorney Reginald Tshabalala, explains it’s not so easy to shift liability when offering a so-called expert service. REGGIE: whether the source of information is TransUnion or not, first of all, accountability, the contracting party to me. So whether accountability gets its information from third party, it doesn't really matter//. At the end of the day, the document is theirs and their own. They must own it. M7 VO: TransUnion responded in writing. They did not specifically answer the questions we posed. But stated the following: “We are confident that we followed all applicable procedures in our data collection...” ANd specifically about the MICAN //ONE WORLD SHINING CASE: “Our review of this matter shows that Accountability may have omitted from their report or presented differently certain information provided by TransUnion that could have offered additional context to the credit decision.” MICHELLE: Accountability's blaming TransUnion, TransUnion is blaming accountability, accountability's blaming us as the customer, and nobody to date has even apologized that this has happened to us or taken responsibility, that the trade references that they gave and the report that they gave to us was an excellent account. But in actual fact, it wasn't. C2M24 10.30 MASA: you've provided this document to your clients. Then you find out that this information is incorrect. Should that not surprise you?. DEVON: That is for the bureau to rectify, it's not for me to justify//. The main thing that I need to get through is that it is powered by the bureau which we state at the bottom. VO: Kemp is adamant that they are covered by their terms and conditions. MASA: Are you passing the buck onto TransUnion because you want to take any responsibility or accountability? DEVON: I cannot take responsibility for information that I did not source MASA: you provided it to your clients as accurate information and you took their money. // We've established now that it's not accurate. DEVON: So that's actually quite want a very stern statement, MASA: FACTUAL a statement, because here is an accountability document that is full of inaccuracies in black and white. DEVON: OK VO: Accountability and TransUnion claim there were discrepancies between the report and the credit application completed by the FAKE company. Tshabalala’s advice is that businesses should scrutinize every detail of every transaction. REGGIE: you are the one who is going to part with goods that you're going to give one credit, it is your responsibility. Don't rely on verification agencies simply because they've got terms and conditions that generally absolve them, // Because if you're going to rely on one verification agency to give you 100 percent information//, you will most likely be disappointed. M14 PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Criminal Syndicates are going all out - creatign a web of deception posing as legitimate companies, getting credit and making off with hundreds of thousands of rands in supplies - without paying a cent. PROMO 2 VO: sophisticated criminal syndicates make off with millions of Rands worth of products using legitimate companies details to get credit – leaving only a trail of deception and suppliers out of pocket. PROMO 3 VO: Who would you hold responsible if you parted supplies worth hundreds of thousands of rands, only to discover the company you had done a credit check on was in fact hijacked by criminals?

metadata.Unique Selling Point: - CAUTIONARY TALE - EXPOSING THE LEVEL OF DECEPTION CREATED BY FRAUDSTERS - NEW CRIME TREND PERFECTLY EXECUTED
metadata.Summary: Criminal Syndicates are going all out to get their hands on products – duping suppliers into giving them credit using legitimate companies details. Suppliers dot all the I’s and cross all the t’s in an attempt to vet these applications – but what do you do when the credit bureaus you employed to check the dodgy company gave the green light to do business with them.
metadata.Further information: OUR CASE STUDY THE VICTIM: MICAN INDUSTRIAL SUPPLIES, a medium sized business THE CON: Supplied PPE goods valued at R585 955.83 to fraudsters in December 2020 on credit. THE ROGUES: Fraudsters posing as ONE WORLD SHINING, a legitimate company with a good credit rating. WHAT HAPPENED: MICAN were contacted by One World Shining (OWS) to supply them with PPE goods. OWS wanted to apply for a credit account and completed a MICAN application form. MICAN in turn sent the credit application details to Accountability – a 3rd party credit check service – who make use of TransUnion Reports and supply clients with a report on an Accountability Document. THE OUTCOME OF THE CREDIT CHECK: OWS passed as a bank code C, For R1.5 million. Rating: Good account, Low Risk. Trade references, were all Excellent! Spending between R350 000 up to R12 million. No judgments or defaults on any trade reference. So MICAN went ahead with order. The goods were delivered and they waited for payments. But almost 6 weeks later they started to get suspicous and uncovered they had been scammed. TRAIL OF DECEIT Not just MICAN. There are at least 3 other comapines that have been scammed. And a further 3 that flagged the applications and did not go through with the purchase order. In the space of a few weeks the FAKE One World Shining applied for credit at the following companies that we know of: • WELDING EQUIPMENT to the value of R400 000 • ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT to the value of R500 000 • SUGAR • OFFICE SUPPLIES • And then MICAN’s PPE worth 600 000 DISCREPANCIES The fraudulent OWS’ company address: 82 Pretoria Road, Sandton. The real OWS company address: 52 Planet Avenue, Unit 21 Chestnut Warehouse, Crown Mines MICAN were told to send the PPE goods to a warehouse and not the Sandton address. The address for the warehouse is; Unit 1, East Borough Business Park, 15 Olympia Street, Eastgate, Sandton. When MICAN went to the warehouse address, they were met by a gentleman by the name of Khaya Radebe, cell phone 067 090 0549, Mr Radebe informed them that he simply works there and has no idea as to who is operating from there, he however signed all 3 of MICAN’s invoices? The property is owned by Tuluze Consulting. CAN THE REAL MR YOUSAF PLEASE STAND UP The details for One World Shining Pty Ltd were hacked(stolen) from a Mr Abdul Qadir Yousaf ID. #: 7611106173187. A certified copy of an ID book is sent to suppliers with the credit applications – the picture in the ID is fake. Mr Yousaf had laid a case at the SAPS in October of 2020 because his details were being used fraudulently. Case #: CAS155:11/2020 at the Langlaagte police station. The fraudsters used a fake ID with the picture of another man in it to get passed the credit checks. The real Mr. Yousaf has agreed to an interview – he says there have been a number of companies contacting him about this con. SKIRTING ACCOUNTABILITY On the company website Accountability describes itself as a web-based service that was created “with the aim of “protecting” businesses by reducing the risk caused by outstanding payments”. Our Value Proposition “By becoming a valued Member of Accountability, you will have access to a variety of services whereby you can accurately determine potential clients’ creditworthiness before extending them the required trade credit.” Mission Statement: Accountability is the dominant web-based service team aiming to protect SME’s and Corporates by providing them with tools to reduce credit risk and report Consumer and Commercial credit behaviour to registered Credit Bureaus. When I spoke to them – they say they merely provide clients with the informationon TransUnion Reports and they are not responsible for that. It seems the fraudsters have managed to get past TransUnion and CIPC and no one is taking responsibility. In Accountability’s T&Cs it states that the subscriber takes all liability. I contacted attorney Reggie Tshabalala who believes it’s not simple when Accountability was providing an expert service. I have sent him the contract and report and will hopefully find out more soonest. COMPANY ID THEFT RIFE Christo Snyman, VP of the International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators (IAFCI) in South Africa, has noted a spike in this type of crime trend. “From our conversations with suppliers, we have discovered that the number of credit applications being made using false or stolen information, has become a massive problem.” Being a victim of identity fraud, which can have a massive negative impact on a company if the situation is not immediately reported and handled correctly. Snyman said that there is a very real need for businesses to become more aware of the prevalence of fraud, and to act when they become aware of fraudulent activity. “Firstly, if you conduct business on credit, never assume the accuracy of a client’s information – always check the validity of the information that they provide. Check that names and contact details are correct, and double check banking details by calling the applicant or customer. In the case of long-standing customers, be especially wary of changes in contact or banking details.” In addition, Snyman said that all businesses must have a policy of reporting any fraudulent activity. “It is very unfortunate that so many companies still choose to let cases of attempted fraud go unreported. Even if it might seem unlikely that the fraudsters will be caught, it is still important to notify police. At the same time, businesses should let other companies in their network know if they become aware of a new scam, or if their identity had been stolen.” INTERVIEWS - MICAN INDUSTRIAL SUPPLIES - SUGAR ON TAP (DIDN’T GET CAUGHT) - THE REAL MR YOUSAF - REGGIE TSHABALALA – ATTORNEY - CHRISTO SNYMAN - International Association of Financial Crimes Investigators - ACCOUNTABILITY - TRACKING AND TRACING ELEMENT
